requirements.statement: For each element that receives focus, taking focus is visible.

citations.quote: Pour chaque élément recevant le focus, la prise de focus vérifie-t-elle une de ces conditions
vérifier que l’indication visuelle de la prise de focus est présente (en agissant sur le contour ou le fond ou les deux) et est suffisamment contrastée (ratio de contraste égal ou supérieur à 3:1)

routes.statement: The browser's native focus style is neither removed nor degraded.

citations.quote: Le style du focus natif du navigateur n’est pas supprimé ou dégradé ;
l’indication visuelle du focus du navigateur ne doit pas être supprimée ou dégradée

routes.statement: A focus style defined by the author is visible and sufficiently contrasted.

citations.quote: Un style du focus défini par l’auteur est visible.
sauf si un style du focus défini par l’auteur est visible et suffisamment contrasté au regard du critère 3.3.

rationale.text: The test accepts two routes: the native focus style kept intact, or an author style that is visible. Deciding that a style is degraded, visible enough, or contrasted at 3:1 against the right colours is judgment in general, so the entry cannot be full. One fault would falsify both routes at once: focusing an element by keyboard changes nothing at all on screen. The custom check looks for it by comparing a screenshot of the viewport with the element focused by Tab and one after blur(). It first proves, on a reference button, that the browser paints focus rings in this setup, and it abstains when the element is partly outside the viewport, very small, transparent, clipped, inside an ancestor that clips its overflow, or covered by another element, and for frames and embedded media. An earlier version made identical screenshots a proof of failure. That was unsound: a page that takes focus back on blur gives two identical screenshots with its focus indicator visible in both. The check now also abstains when focus is still on the element or on another element after blur, when the DOM changed during blur, or when an animation is still running. These guards are necessary but do not prove that the second screenshot shows the page as it looks without focus. A script can react to blur without touching the DOM, for example by redrawing a canvas, and an indicator added on focus and kept after blur shows in both screenshots although the element did show focus. I cannot state and verify every assumption of the technique, so the link is evidence only and the entry is none. Raising it would need a way to show that the two screenshots differ only by the element's focus state: for example, that no focus, blur, focusin or focusout listener exists on the element, its ancestors, the document or the window, and that the page in its focused state, compared with the page before the element ever took focus, also shows no change; plus corpus cases for a page that refocuses on blur, a truly removed indicator, an ordinary author indicator and an indicator kept after blur. Its scope is partial: it follows only the Tab order, not elements that take focus only from a pointer. No axe rule is tagged. Applicability is judgment: elements can be made focusable by script and the glossary includes focus given by pointer, so the absence of any element receiving focus is not certain from static code. Needs lists keyboard, since the check needs the keyboard pass.

citations.quote: pour chaque élément recevant le focus, la prise de focus est-elle visible
En atteignant l’élément par la touche tabulation ou majuscule + tabulation ;
Si c’est le cas pour chaque élément susceptible de recevoir le focus, **le test est validé**.
